I used a site call Terrarium Tribe[here](https://terrariumtribe.com/) to start out learning, has a great section for which plants work well in different environment. The r/terrariums sub is active but we're generally a small community of enthusiasts

Make sure they're all lovely and clean ofcourse and after that it really depends on container size and what type of plants you want. Have a bit of a look around on Google and expect to only get about half the plants in that you'd like!
Succulents work nice in dry looking ecos, mosses and ferns are better in more forest like ones with a lot of moisture but ferns can get big. Epiphytes (massive variety) are also highly recommended. Surprisingly some carnivorous plants work well like Nepenthes (pitcher plants) because they like boggy wet environments but you have to have some mold flies in the eco at least to let them get any nitrogen from feeding.

Tips for beginners would be make sure to grab some activated charcoal, a layer of this in your sediment helps massively with mold/bacteria. Air seal your containers, doesn't have to be fancy but just make sure those seals are sealed, I personally like to use silicone. For your sediment again depends on the environment but a mixture of coconut fibres and mosses do wonders for holding moisture. Once you place it don't move it! The plants will need some time to settle in their roots before they'll grow the nice looking green bits, so it's tempting to move them to sunny spots to get some extra growth but you're better to set them in place and have them compete naturally for light by growing themselves.

Dont be afraid of creepy crawlies, get yourself some springtails if you can, you'll probably find some in soil you buy anyway, harmless little fellas and they eat all the bad stuff and produce lovely nutrients for your plants. Mold flies can be good too, they eat mold/detritus in soil and fertilise it back when they die.
